title: Matching is case-sensitive; `LIKE` has no default escape
description: `LIKE`, `CONTAINS`, `STARTSWITH`, `ENDSWITH`, `POSITION` and `REGEXP_LIKE` are case-sensitive; `ILIKE`, `REGEXP_LIKE(…, 'i')` and a `COLLATE 'en-ci'` are not. Without a collation, strings compare by code point (`'B' < 'a'`, `'é' > 'z'`), which is UTF-8 byte order.

A backslash is not an escape in `LIKE` without an `ESCAPE` clause: `'a_c' LIKE 'a\\_c'` is FALSE. With `ESCAPE '\\'`, a pattern ending in a lone escape matches it literally. `%` and `_` match newlines.
reference: `case_sensitivity: CASE_SENSITIVE`, code point order: native. sverify's SQL writes `ESCAPE '\\'` and appends a backslash to a pattern ending in an odd number of them (`like_pattern`).

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT contains('Abc', 'a'), startswith('Abc', 'a'), endswith('abC', 'c'), position('A' IN 'abc'), regexp_like('Abc', 'a.*'), regexp_like('Abc', 'a.*', 'i')

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
